info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 2 at 1:38PM EST until November 2 at 3:45PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 3:45 PM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 3:45 PM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Brevard County in east central Florida...

* Until 345 PM EST.

* At 138 PM EST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
15 and 20 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
of 1 to 3 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Palm Bay, Melbourne, Malabar, Indialantic, Camp Holly Fish Camp,
West Melbourne, Melbourne Beach, Grant-Valkaria, Micco, Melbourne
Village, June Park, Melbourne Airport, Spessard Holland Park,
Melbourne Shores and Floridana Beach.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown. Be aware of your surroundings and do not
drive on flooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

info.description: Sedgwick County Emergency Management will NOT be testing the Outdoor Warning Sirens Today. Sedgwick County outdoor warning sirens are tested every Monday at Noon, except Holidays and when threatening weather is present. Outdoor warning sirens are designed to be an early warning device primarily for persons who are outside away from the television and or radio. Remember, when the outdoor warning sirens sound, Take cover, Tune in to local media, Take action.
info.instruction: Emergency Management officials highly recommend citizens keep a NOAA weather radio in their homes, preferably in the bedroom, with a tone alert for those times when you are not monitoring public media. This broadcast originates from Sedgwick County Emergency Management located at seven fourteen North Main, Wichita Kansas. WPMQ three ninety one. No action required test only.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 2 at 12:10PM EST until November 2 at 1:45PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

parameter.name: NWSheadline
parameter.value: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 145 PM EST THIS AFTERNOON FOR SOUTHEASTERN BREVARD AND NORTHEASTERN INDIAN RIVER COUNTIES

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 1:45 PM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 1:45 PM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
At 1210 PM EST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 6
and 8 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 3 to
5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sebastian, Indian River Shores, Roseland, Sebastian Highlands,
Sebastian Inlet, Barefoot Bay, Wabasso, Sebastian Inlet State Park,
Micco, Orchid, North Beach, Wabasso Beach and Disneys Vero Beach
Resort.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown. Be aware of your surroundings and do not
drive on flooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 2 at 11:35AM EST until November 2 at 1:45PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

parameter.name: NWSheadline
parameter.value: FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY FOR WEST MELBOURNE, PALM BAY, AND GRANT-VALKARIA

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY this area til 1:45 PM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY is in effect for this area until 1:45 PM EST. This is an extremely dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Brevard County in east central Florida...

* Until 145 PM EST.

* At 1135 AM EST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
15 and 20 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
of 2 to 4 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
already occurring.

FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for West Melbourne, Palm Bay, and
Grant-Valkaria. This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK
HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER
GROUND NOW! Life threatening flash flooding of low water
crossings, small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Palm Bay, Melbourne, Malabar, Indialantic, Camp Holly Fish Camp,
West Melbourne, Melbourne Beach, Grant-Valkaria, Micco, Melbourne
Village, June Park, Melbourne Airport, Spessard Holland Park,
Melbourne Shores and Floridana Beach.
info.instruction:
Move to higher ground now! This is an extremely dangerous and
life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are
fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

Turn around, don't drown. Be aware of your surroundings and do not
drive on flooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 2 at 11:12AM EST until November 2 at 1:15PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 1:15 PM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 1:15 PM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central St. Lucie County in east central Florida...

* Until 115 PM EST.

* At 1112 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 4 and 8 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Fort Pierce, White City, Fort Pierce South, Fort Pierce North,
Saint Lucie West, Indian River Estates, Port Saint Lucie River
Park, Saint Lucie Airport, Saint Lucie Village, Saint Lucie,
Collins Park Estates, Carlton and Tradition Field.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 2 at 10:45AM EST until November 2 at 1:45PM EST by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 1:45 PM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 1:45 PM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWTBW

The National Weather Service in Tampa Bay Ruskin has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Hardee County in central Florida...
Northern DeSoto County in south central Florida...
Southwestern Highlands County in south central Florida...

* Until 145 PM EST.

* At 1045 AM EST, Emergency management reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 7 and 11
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 3
inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Multiple emergency management agencies have reported
flooded roads, and water in or approaching homes and
structures.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sebring, Avon Park, Arcadia, Wauchula, Lake Placid, Sylvan Shores,
Sebring Regional Airport, Lake Istokpoga, Southeast Arcadia,
Sweetwater, Zolfo Springs, Crewsville, Lake Josephine, Sebring
Shores, Avon Park Executive Airport, Placid Lakes, Gardner,
Brownville, Archbold and Lorida.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Coconino County in north central Arizona... Navajo County in north central Arizona... * Until 200 PM MST Monday. * At 743 AM MST, a river gauge on the Little Colorado River at Winslow has rapidly risen to near Major flood stage due to upstream heavy rainfall. Additional rises to above Major flood stage are forecast shortly, with flooding impacts to Ames Acres and Bushman Acres in Winslow. Flash flooding is already occurring. HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash flooding. SOURCE...River gauge reported. IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses. * For Little Colorado at Winslow: At 7:00am MST the stage was 24.81 feet. Flood Stage is 19.0 feet. Forecast: A crest of 46 feet is expected around 1:00am MST Monday. Impacts: At 22.0 feet: Lowland flooding on right bank. Damage on left bank to Ames Acres and Bushman Acres in the event of levee failure. At 25.0 feet: Levee is overtopped. Major flooding of portions of Winslow including Ames Acres and Bushman Acres. Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Winslow, Leupp, Birdsprings, Sunrise, Bushman Acres and Homolovi Ruins State Park. This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds... Homolovi State Park Campground. This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers... Little Colorado River. Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become flooded as well. Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads. Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded roads. info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 2 at 7:43AM MST until November 2 at 2:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 2:00 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 2:00 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Navajo County in north central Arizona...

* Until 200 PM MST Monday.

* At 743 AM MST, a river gauge on the Little Colorado River at
Winslow has rapidly risen to near Major flood stage due to upstream
heavy rainfall. Additional rises to above Major flood stage are
forecast shortly, with flooding impacts to Ames Acres and Bushman
Acres in Winslow. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 7:00am MST the stage was 24.81 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 46 feet is expected around 1:00am MST Monday.
Impacts:
At 22.0 feet: Lowland flooding on right bank. Damage on left bank
to Ames Acres and Bushman Acres in the event of levee failure.
At 25.0 feet: Levee is overtopped. Major flooding of portions of
Winslow including Ames Acres and Bushman Acres.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Winslow, Leupp, Birdsprings, Sunrise, Bushman Acres and Homolovi
Ruins State Park.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Homolovi State Park Campground.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Little Colorado River.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Brevard County in east central Florida...

* Until 1145 AM EST.

* At 934 AM EST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
12 and 15 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
of 3 to 5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing.

FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for West Melbourne and Palm Bay. This is a
PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER
GROUND NOW! Life threatening flash flooding of low water
crossings, small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Palm Bay, Melbourne, Malabar, Indialantic, Camp Holly Fish Camp,
West Melbourne, Melbourne Beach, Grant-Valkaria, Micco, Melbourne
Village, June Park, Melbourne Airport, Spessard Holland Park,
Melbourne Shores and Floridana Beach.
info.instruction:
Move to higher ground now! This is an extremely dangerous and
life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are
fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 11:00 AM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 11:00 AM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWTBW

The National Weather Service in Tampa Bay Ruskin has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern Hardee County in central Florida...
Northern DeSoto County in south central Florida...
Northwestern Highlands County in south central Florida...

* Until 1100 AM EST.

* At 928 AM EST, Emergency Management in DeSoto County reported
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Water
has been reported entering structures. Between 5 and 9 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sebring, Avon Park, Arcadia, Wauchula, Southeast Arcadia, Sebring
Regional Airport, Sweetwater, Zolfo Springs, Crewsville, Gardner,
Brownville, Sebring Shores, Avon Park Executive Airport, Lake
Josephine and Limestone.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

parameter.name: NWSheadline
parameter.value: FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY FOR WEST MELBOURNE AND PALM BAY

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY this area til 9:45 AM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY is in effect for this area until 9:45 AM EST. This is an extremely dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Brevard County in east central Florida...

* Until 945 AM EST.

* At 756 AM EST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
8 and 12 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
4 to 6 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for West Melbourne and Palm Bay. This is a
PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER
GROUND NOW! Life threatening flash flooding of low water
crossings, small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Palm Bay, Melbourne, Malabar, Indialantic, Camp Holly Fish Camp,
West Melbourne, Melbourne Beach, Grant-Valkaria, Micco, Melbourne
Village, June Park, Melbourne Airport, Spessard Holland Park,
Melbourne Shores and Floridana Beach.
info.instruction:
Move to higher ground now! This is an extremely dangerous and
life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are
fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 9:45 AM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 9:45 AM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Brevard County in east central Florida...

* Until 945 AM EST.

* At 727 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 8 and 10 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Palm Bay, Melbourne, Rockledge, Satellite Beach, Malabar,
Indialantic, Camp Holly Fish Camp, Patrick Space Force Base,
Merritt Island, Barefoot Bay, West Melbourne, Indian Harbour Beach,
Melbourne Beach, South Patrick Shores, Suntree, Grant-Valkaria,
Viera, Micco and Palm Shores.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 2 at 3:55AM MST until November 2 at 7:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 7:00 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 7:00 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 700 AM MST.

* At 355 AM MST, a gauge on the Moenkopi Wash reported a rise well
above Major flood stage from heavy rain in the Moenkopi Wash basin.
Additional rises are possible. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Moenkopi Wash.

* For Moenkopi Wash at Moenkopi Wash Near Tuba City:
At 2:45am MST the stage was 33.74 feet.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 27.0 feet: At 27.0 feet water begins to encroach on homes in
lower Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Moenkopi.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Fivemile Wash, Hamblin Wash, Begashibito Wash and Moenkopi Wash.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Brevard County in east central Florida...

* Until 745 AM EST.

* At 444 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 6 and 8 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Palm Bay, Melbourne, Rockledge, Satellite Beach, Malabar,
Indialantic, Camp Holly Fish Camp, Patrick Space Force Base,
Merritt Island, Barefoot Bay, West Melbourne, Indian Harbour Beach,
Melbourne Beach, South Patrick Shores, Suntree, Grant-Valkaria,
Viera, Micco and Palm Shores.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 8:00 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Navajo County in north central Arizona...

* Until 800 AM MST.

* At 206 AM MST, a river gauge on the Little Colorado River has
rapidly risen above Moderate flood stage due to upstream heavy rain
fall. Further rises to above Major flood stages are expected
shortly, with flooding impacts to Ames Acres and Bushman Acres in
Winslow. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 1:00am MST the stage was 23.05 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest over 40 feet is possible by 1:00pm MST Tuesday.
Impacts:
At 22.0 feet: Lowland flooding on right bank. Damage on left bank
to Ames Acres and Bushman Acres in the event of levee failure.
At 25.0 feet: Levee is overtopped. Major flooding of portions of
Winslow including Ames Acres and Bushman Acres.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Winslow, Leupp, Birdsprings, Sunrise, Bushman Acres and Homolovi
Ruins State Park.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Homolovi State Park Campground.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Little Colorado River.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 2 at 12:37AM MST until November 2 at 4:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 4:00 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 4:00 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 400 AM MST.

* At 1237 AM MST, a gauge on the Moenkopi Wash reported a rise above
action stage from heavy rain in the Moenkopi Wash basin. Further
rapid rises are expected, with water levels expected to exceed
major flood stage. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Moenkopi Wash.

* For Moenkopi Wash at Moenkopi Wash Near Tuba City:
At 10:45pm MST the stage was 26.77 feet.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 28.74 feet is expected at 6:00am MST Monday.
Impacts:
At 27.0 feet: At 27.0 feet water begins to encroach on homes in
lower Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Moenkopi.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Fivemile Wash, Hamblin Wash, Begashibito Wash and Moenkopi Wash.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.headline: Tornado Warning issued November 1 at 11:55PM CST until November 2 at 12:30AM CST by NWS Amarillo TX

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: TORNADO WARNING in this area til 12:30 AM CST. Take shelter now. Check media.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: TORNADO WARNING in this area until 12:30 AM CST. Take shelter now in a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Check media.

info.description:
TORAMA

The National Weather Service in Amarillo has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Northwestern Texas County in the panhandle of Oklahoma...

* Until 1230 AM CST.

* At 1155 PM CST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a
tornado was located 6 miles north of Eva, or 29 miles northwest of
Guymon, moving northeast at 45 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Eva.
info.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

Tornadoes are difficult to observe at night. Take cover now!

info.headline: Tornado Warning issued November 1 at 11:18PM CST until November 1 at 11:45PM CST by NWS Amarillo TX

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: TORNADO WARNING in this area til 11:45 PM CST. Take shelter now. Check media.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: TORNADO WARNING in this area until 11:45 PM CST. Take shelter now in a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Check media.

info.description:
TORAMA

The National Weather Service in Amarillo has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Northeastern Cimarron County in the panhandle of Oklahoma...
Northwestern Texas County in the panhandle of Oklahoma...

* Until 1145 PM CST.

* At 1118 PM CST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a
tornado was located 10 miles northeast of Keyes, or 25 miles
northeast of Boise City, moving northeast at 55 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Sturgis.
info.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

Tornadoes are difficult to observe at night. Take cover now!

parameter.value: Servicio Nacional de Meteorologia: AVISO DE TORNADO en efecto hasta las 11:45 PM CST. Busque refugio ahora en un sotano o en el interior de un cuarto en el nivel mas bajo de un edificio seguro. Si esta al aire libre, en una casa movil, o en un vehiculo, debe ir al edificio seguro mas cercano y protegerse de proyectiles. Consulte los medios informativos.

parameter.value: NWS: TORNADO WARNING in this area til 11:45 PM CST. Take shelter now. Check media.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: TORNADO WARNING in this area until 11:45 PM CST. Take shelter now in a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Check media.

info.description:
TORAMA

The National Weather Service in Amarillo has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Southeastern Hartley County in the panhandle of Texas...
Northeastern Oldham County in the panhandle of Texas...

* Until 1145 PM CST.

* At 1112 PM CST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a
tornado was located 13 miles north of Adrian, or 22 miles northwest
of Vega, moving northeast at 55 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Channing.
info.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

Tornadoes are difficult to observe at night. Take cover now!

info.instruction:
19,000 Blk Hwy 145  - PRE-EVACUATION ALERT

PRE-EVACUATION ALERT. Montezuma County Sheriff issuing PRE-EVACUATION ORDER for residents 19,700 blk to 19,900 blk of HWY 145. Be prepared to evacuate when the order is given. 

This is due to the Dolores River rising based on water runoff due to excessive rain. Predictions of river rising may cause serious flooding in this area. 

There is no mandatory evacuation order yet, conditions are actively changing, and you should be ready to leave at a moment's notice. If you need extra time to evacuate, or have pets, livestock, or medical needs, consider leaving now. Pack your Go-Bag and important items. Monitor local updates via [radio station / emergency alert link / social media page].

A MANDATORY EVACUATION has been ordered due to a reported dam breach at Chama Land.
Evacuation Area: From the Elkhorn Restaurant south to Unser's Highway 64 84 Mile Post 164 
Residents and businesses within the affected area are directed to EVACUATE IMMEDIATELY.
 IMPORTANT

info.headline: Tornado Warning issued November 1 at 9:29PM MST until November 1 at 10:00PM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: TORNADO WARNING in this area til 10:00 PM MST. Take shelter now. Check media.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: TORNADO WARNING in this area until 10:00 PM MST. Take shelter now in a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Check media.

info.description:
TORABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
East Central Quay County in east central New Mexico...

* Until 1000 PM MST.

* At 929 PM MST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located 6 miles northeast of San Jon, or 25 miles east of
Tucumcari, moving northeast at 50 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of East Central Quay County.
info.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

Tornadoes are difficult to observe at night. Take cover now!

Si esta al aire libre, en una casa movil, o en un vehiculo, debe ir al edificio seguro mas cercano y protegerse de proyectiles. Consulte los medios informativos.

parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 12:00 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 12:00 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Sand Stone burn scar in...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* Until midnight MST.

* At 801 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Sand Stone Burn Scar. Up to 1.25 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result
in debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Sand Stone Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Sand Stone Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Round Valley and Sugarloaf Mountain.
info.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Sand Stone Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be
anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in
places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 8:52PM EST until November 1 at 11:15PM EST by NWS Miami FL

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 11:15 PM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 11:15 PM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Palm Beach County in southeastern Florida...

* Until 1115 PM EST.

* At 852 PM EST, The public reported flash flooding in communities
near Military Trail road, with water entering homes. Roads and
streets nearby Okeechobee Road and Military trail are reported to
be impassable. Between 9 and 12 inches of rain have fallen. The
expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to 1.5 inches in 1 hour. Additional
rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the warned area.
Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Public reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
West Palm Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, Riviera Beach, North Palm
Beach, Lake Park, Haverhill, Cloud Lake, Schall Circle, Port Of
Palm Beach, Golden Lakes, Lake Belvedere Estates, Royal Palm
Estates, President Donald J. Trump International Airport, Downtown
West Palm Beach, Gun Club Estates, Mangonia Park, Glen Ridge,
Lakeside Green and Cypress Lakes.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

dangers of flooding.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 7:50PM EST until November 1 at 9:15PM EST by NWS Miami FL

parameter.name: NWSheadline
parameter.value: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 915 PM EST THIS EVENING FOR NORTHEASTERN PALM BEACH COUNTY

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 9:15 PM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 9:15 PM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
At 750 PM EST, The public reported flash flooding in communities near
Military Trail road, with water starting to enter homes. Roads and
streets nearby Okeechobee Road and Military trail are reported to be
impassable. Between 7 and 10 inches of rain have fallen. The expected
rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts
of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash
flooding.

SOURCE...Public reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
West Palm Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, Riviera Beach, North Palm
Beach, Lake Park, Haverhill, Cloud Lake, Schall Circle, Port Of
Palm Beach, Golden Lakes, Lake Belvedere Estates, Royal Palm
Estates, President Donald J. Trump International Airport, Downtown
West Palm Beach, Gun Club Estates, Mangonia Park, Glen Ridge,
Lakeside Green and Cypress Lakes.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 1:00 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Moenkopi Wash in Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 100 AM MST Monday.

* At 458 PM MST, a gauge on the Moenkopi Wash reported a rise above
action stage from heavy rain in the Moenkopi Wash basin. Further
rises are expected, with water levels expected to exceed major
flood stage. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Moenkopi Wash.

* For Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City:
At 4:45pm MST the stage was 26.0 feet.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 29.45 feet is expected at 5:00am MST Monday.
Impacts:
At 27.0 feet: At 27.0 feet water begins to encroach on homes in
lower Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Moenkopi.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Fivemile Wash, Hamblin Wash, Begashibito Wash and Moenkopi Wash.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

parameter.value: SNM: AVISO DE INUNDACIONES REPENTINAS hasta 1:00 AM MST. Evite areas inundadas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: Servicio Nacional de Meteorologia: AVISO DE INUNDACIONES REPENTINAS en efecto para esta area hasta las 1:00 AM MST. Esta es una situacion peligrosa y amenaza la vida. No intente viajar a menos que sea para abandonar un area propensa a inundaciones o bajo una orden de desalojo.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Moenkopi Wash in Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 100 AM MST Monday.

* At 458 PM MST, a gauge on the Moenkopi Wash reported a rise above
action stage from heavy rain in the Moenkopi Wash basin. Further
rises are expected, with water levels expected to exceed major
flood stage. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Moenkopi Wash.

* For Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City:
At 4:45pm MST the stage was 26.0 feet.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 29.45 feet is expected at 5:00am MST Monday.
Impacts:
At 27.0 feet: At 27.0 feet water begins to encroach on homes in
lower Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Moenkopi.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Fivemile Wash, Hamblin Wash, Begashibito Wash and Moenkopi Wash.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 3:52PM MST until November 1 at 10:30PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 10:30 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 10:30 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Paria River in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 1030 PM MST Sunday.

* At 352 PM MST, a river gauge on the Paria River reported a rapid
rise from heavy rain over the Paria River drainage basin. Flood
waters will proceed down the Paria River drainage this evening
reaching Lees Ferry between about 8 to 10 PM MST.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Paria River.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Paria River.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lees Ferry and Vermilion Cliffs National Monument.

This includes the Colorado River near mile marker 0.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Lees Ferry Camp Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Colorado River and Paria River.
info.instruction:
Get out of the Paria River slot canyon! Flood waters will flow down
the Paria River, reaching the confluence with the Colorado River at
Lees Ferry around 8:00 to 10:00 PM MST.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Get out of washes and creeks if you are camping or hiking! Flooding
is occurring or imminent and will inundate creeks and washes.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 3:41PM MST until November 1 at 8:30PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 8:30 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 8:30 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 830 PM MST.

* At 341 PM MST, the river guage on Oak Creek near Sedona remained
near flood stage, with futher rises expected. Oak Creek at
Cornville remained above moderate flood stage. emergency management
has reported flooding around Tlaquepaque in Sedona. Flash flooding
is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* For Oak Creek at Cornville:
At 3:00pm the stage was 16.94 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.0 feet.
Forecast: A is expected at late this evening around 19 feet.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Inundation begins to affect fish hatchery across from
gauge site.
At 21.0 feet: Stream reaches bridge at Page Springs Rd.
...
For Oak Creek at Sedona:
At 2:45pm the stage was 13.93 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest is expected late this evening near 18 feet.
Impacts:
At 13.0 feet: Stream reaches terrace under Tlaquepaque bridge. Low
water crossings closed.
At 14.0 feet: Flood stage. Several islands downstream in Sedona
evacuated. Minor flooding of access roads, buildings, and
residences along Oak Creek.
At 16.0 feet: Flooding begins at Rancho Sedona RV Park on Bear
Wallow Lane, Trails End Drive, Oak Creek Mobilodge, Poco Diablo
Resort on Sycamore Road and Oak Creek Cliffs Drive, and Chavez
Crossing Campground.
At 18.0 feet: Minor damage to shops and galleries near the
Tlaquepaque bridge.
At 20.0 feet: Major flooding to mobile homes downstream from the
Tlaquepaque bridge and access roads along Oak Creek through Sedona.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sedona, Cornville, Jordan, Page Springs, Bignotti, Indian Gardens,
Pine Flats, Uptown Sedona, Sedona Airport, Red Rock State Park,
Slide Rock State Park, West Fork of Oak Creek, Red Rock-Secret
Mountain Wilderness, Cathedral Rock and Oak Creek Vista Overlook.

This includes the following highways...
State Route 179 between mile markers 310 and 313. State Route 89A
between mile markers 373 and 384...and between mile markers 386 and
390.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Manzanita Campground, Pine Flat Campground, Cave Springs Campground
and Windmill Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Pumphouse Wash, Slide Rock, Encinoso, Grasshopper Point, Midgely
Bridge, Buddha Beach "Red Rock Crossing", Crescent Moon Ranch and
Mormons Crossing.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Oak Creek.
info.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 5:05PM EST until November 1 at 6:30PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 6:30 PM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 6:30 PM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Okeechobee County in east central Florida...

* Until 630 PM EST.

* At 505 PM EST, local law enforcement reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 5 and 9 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Treasure Island, Okeechobee, Four Seasons Estates, Taylor Creek,
Whispering Pines, Okeechobee Airport and Basswood Estates.

Law enforcement reports portions of SR 70 and US 441 in and around
the City of Okeechobee are impassable. Motorists should avoid these
roads. Water was also entering structures.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 2:24PM MST until November 1 at 8:30PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 8:30 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 8:30 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Navajo County in north central Arizona...
Apache County in northeastern Arizona...

* Until 830 PM MST Sunday.

* At 224 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Chinle, Fort Defiance, Window Rock, Many Farms, Lukachukai, Tsaile,
St. Michaels, Sanders, Houck, Round Rock, Dennehotso, Chilchinbeto,
Rough Rock, Teec Nos Pos, Sawmill, Red Mesa, Del Muerto, Black
Mesa, Querino and Rock Point.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 160 between mile markers 401 and 470. Interstate 40 between
mile markers 323 and 359. Highway 191 161 between mile markers 366
and 368. State Route 264 between mile markers 455 and 475. Highway
191 between mile markers 374 and 390...and between mile markers 438
and 510.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Cottonwood Campground, Wagon Wheel Campground, Tsegi Overlook,
Junction Overlook, White House Overlook, Antelope House Overlook,
Face Rock Overlook and Spider Rock Overlook.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Oraibi Wash, Kinlichee Creek, Standing Redrock Creek, Lizard Wash,
Teec Nos Pos Wash, Piney Hill Creek,  Canyon del Muerto,
Wheatfields Creek, Puerco River, Cienega Creek, Dinnebito Wash,
Chinle Creek, Polacca Wash, Lukachukai Creek, Toh Dahstini Wash and
Nazlini Wash.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 5:15 PM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Okeechobee County in east central Florida...

* Until 515 PM EST.

* At 406 PM EST, local law enforcement reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 5 and 9 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Treasure Island, Okeechobee, Four Seasons Estates, Taylor Creek,
Whispering Pines, Okeechobee Airport and Basswood Estates.

Law enforcement reports portions of SR 70 and US 441 in and around
the City of Okeechobee are impassable. Motorists should avoid these
roads. Water was also entering structures.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Treasure Island, Okeechobee, Four Seasons Estates, Taylor Creek,
Whispering Pines, Okeechobee Airport and Basswood Estates.

the City of Okeechobee are impassable. Motorists should avoid these
roads. Water was also entering structures.
info.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 515 PM MST.

* At 153 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches
of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* For Wet Beaver Creek at Wet Beaver Creek Near Rimrock:

Flood Stage is 9.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest is expected Sunday evening.
Impacts:
At 8.0 feet: Low water crossings impassable, water begins to exceed
banks and inundate low lying areas.
At 9.5 feet: Water begins to impact residential structures along Rim
Rock Drive and Beaver Vista in Lake Montezuma.
At 10.5 feet: Water likely impacting first ground level of residences
along Rim Rock Drive and Beaver Vista, water begins to directly
impact Rim Rock Drive and Beaver Vista.
At 12.0 feet: Widespread inundation of residences along Wet Beaver
Creek.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lake Montezuma, Rimrock, Montezuma Castle National Monument,
McGuireville, Montezuma Well, Lawrence Crossing, Crane Petroglyph
Heritage Site, Bell Crossing/The Crack and Wet Beaver Wilderness.

This includes Interstate 17 between mile markers 291 and 293.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Wet Beaver Creek Campground.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Wet Beaver Creek Day Use Area and Bell Crossing "The Crack".

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Rarick Canyon, Long Canyon, Walker Creek, Beaver Creek and Russell
Wash.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

* At 153 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches
of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* For Wet Beaver Creek at Wet Beaver Creek Near Rimrock:

Flood Stage is 9.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest is expected Sunday evening.
Impacts:
At 8.0 feet: Low water crossings impassable, water begins to exceed
banks and inundate low lying areas.
At 9.5 feet: Water begins to impact residential structures along Rim
Rock Drive and Beaver Vista in Lake Montezuma.
At 10.5 feet: Water likely impacting first ground level of residences
along Rim Rock Drive and Beaver Vista, water begins to directly
impact Rim Rock Drive and Beaver Vista.
At 12.0 feet: Widespread inundation of residences along Wet Beaver
Creek.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lake Montezuma, Rimrock, Montezuma Castle National Monument,
McGuireville, Montezuma Well, Lawrence Crossing, Crane Petroglyph
Heritage Site, Bell Crossing/The Crack and Wet Beaver Wilderness.

This includes Interstate 17 between mile markers 291 and 293.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Wet Beaver Creek Campground.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Wet Beaver Creek Day Use Area and Bell Crossing "The Crack".

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Rarick Canyon, Long Canyon, Walker Creek, Beaver Creek and Russell
Wash.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext

info.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern San Juan County in northwestern New Mexico...

* Until 830 PM MST Sunday.

* At 146 PM MST, Emergency Management reported elevated flows in
arroyos and washes, including washed out roads and water over roads
in the warned area. Between 0.5 and 0.75 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Farmington, Bloomfield, Aztec, Kirtland, Turley, Archuleta, Upper
Fruitland, Fruitland and Nenahnezad.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 550 between Mile Markers 151 and 160...and between Mile
Markers 163 and 165...and near Mile Marker 167. Highway 64 between
Mile Markers 32 and 82...and between Mile Markers 85 and 86.

This includes the following low water crossings...
West Navajo Street at Farmington Glade Arroyo and Hubbard Street at
Hood Arroyo.

This includes the following recreation areas...
Dunes Recreation Area, Negro Canyon Recreation Area, Simon Canyon
Recreation Area, Hammond Point San Juan River Access, Pine Point
River Access and San Juan River Access.
info.instruction:
Do not enter or cross flowing water or water of unknown depth. Turn
around don't drown!

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 1:39PM MST until November 1 at 3:45PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 3:45 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 3:45 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Pima County in southeastern Arizona...
South Central Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 345 PM MST.

* At 139 PM MST, Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen over the
last 3 hours. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Runoff from the rainfall is expected to
continue and area washes are still running, so the Flash Flood
Warning has been extended.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Tucson, Catalina, Oro Valley, Marana, Oracle, Casas Adobes, Drexel
Heights, Flowing Wells, Saddlebrooke, South Tucson, Three Points,
Saddlebrooke Ranch, Pascua Pueblo Yaqui Reservation, Tortolita, San
Xavier Community, Tucson Mountain Park, Saguaro National Park West,
Tucson Estates, Valencia West and Catalina Foothills.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Manville Rd at Brawley Wash, 1st Ave north of Fort Lowell Rd, Stone
Ave at Mabel St, Twin Peaks Rd between Sanders and Sandario,
Silverbell Rd near Ina Rd, Camino De La Tierra at the Rillito River,
Camino de Oeste from Sweetwater to Gates Pass, Ironwood Hills Dr from
Shannon to Camino de Oeste, Mark Rd from Jeffery Rd to Los Reales Rd,
Mission Rd from Valencia Rd to San Xavier Rd, Overton Rd at Canada
del Oro, Sunset Rd west of Camino de Oeste, E Wilds Rd at the Canada
del Oro and Black Wash at S Camino de Oeste.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Chirreon Wash, Guild Wash, Oro, Caada del, Alambre Wash, Brawley
Wash, Big Wash, Demetrie Wash, Cerro Prieto Wash, Rillito River,
Altar Wash, West Branch Santa Cruz River, Old Junction Wash, Soto
Wash, Banner Wash, Santa Cruz River, Chico, Arroyo, Chalk Creek,
Mendoza Wash, Indian Well Wash, Blanco Wash, Champurrado Wash,
Robles Wash, Los, Sutherland Wash and South Mendoza Wash.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 1:22PM MST until November 1 at 4:45PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 4:45 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 4:45 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 445 PM MST.

* At 122 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned
area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen. Flash
flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Bagdad, Congress, Yarnell, Wilhoit, Peeples Valley, Highland Pines,
Hillside, Wickenburg Ranch, Iron Springs, Kirkland, Skull Valley,
Copper Basin, Hawkins, Wildwood Estates, Bagdad Airport, Stanton
and Wagoner.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 93 between mile markers 149 and 196. State Route 96 between
mile markers 0 and 21. State Route 71 between mile markers 90 and
109. State Route 89 between mile markers 258 and 302. State Route 97
between mile markers 156 and 166.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Yavapai Campground, Yavapai Campground, Alto Pit OHV and Cayuse
Picnic Area.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Orofino Wash, Miller Creek, Yarnell Creek, Amazon Gulch, Hassayampa
River, Santa Maria River, Skull Valley Wash, Ash Creek, Iron
Springs Wash, Boulder Creek, Granite Creek, Bottleneck Wash,
Buckhorn Creek, Martinez Creek, Weaver Creek, Little Buckhorn
Creek, Whipsaw Creek and Cellar Springs Creek.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 1:22PM MST until November 1 at 4:45PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: SNM: AVISO DE INUNDACIONES REPENTINAS hasta 4:45 PM MST. Evite areas inundadas.

parameter.value: Servicio Nacional de Meteorologia: AVISO DE INUNDACIONES REPENTINAS en efecto para esta area hasta las 4:45 PM MST. Esta es una situacion peligrosa y amenaza la vida. No intente viajar a menos que sea para abandonar un area propensa a inundaciones o bajo una orden de desalojo.

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 4:15 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 4:15 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 415 PM MST.

* At 1234 PM MST, an automated stream gauge on Oak Creek near
Cornville has surpassed its previous record set in 1993. Between
2.5 and 4 inches of rain have fallen across the upper Oak Creek
watershed. Moderate rainfall continues at this time and water
levels are expected to continue rising this afternoon. Flash
flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* For Oak Creek at Cornville:

At 12:00pm the stage was 19.56 feet. This has surpassed the previous
record stage set in 1993.
Flood Stage is 8.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest is expected Sunday afternoon.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Inundation begins to affect fish hatchery across from
gauge site.
At 21.0 feet: Stream reaches bridge at Page Springs Rd.
...

For Oak Creek at Oak Creek at Sedona:

At 11:45am the stage was 12.44 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest is expected Sunday afternoon.
Impacts:
At 13.0 feet: Stream reaches terrace under Tlaquepaque bridge. Low
water crossings closed.
At 14.0 feet: Flood stage. Several islands downstream in Sedona
evacuated. Minor flooding of access roads, buildings, and residences
along Oak Creek.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sedona, Cornville, Jordan, Page Springs, Indian Gardens, Pine
Flats, Uptown Sedona, Red Rock State Park, Slide Rock State Park,
West Fork of Oak Creek, Red Rock-Secret Mountain Wilderness,
Cathedral Rock and Oak Creek Vista Overlook.

This includes the following highways...
State Route 179 between mile markers 310 and 313. State Route 89A
between mile markers 373 and 390.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Manzanita Campground, Pine Flat Campground, Cave Springs Campground
and Windmill Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Pumphouse Wash, Slide Rock, Encinoso, Grasshopper Point, Midgely
Bridge, Buddha Beach "Red Rock Crossing", Crescent Moon Ranch and
Mormons Crossing.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
West Fork Oak Creek and Oak Creek.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 12:34PM MST until November 1 at 8:30PM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 8:30 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 8:30 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central San Juan County in northwestern New Mexico...

* Until 830 PM MST Sunday.

* At 1234 PM MST, Emergency Managers reported Highway 170 washed out
between mile markers 3 and 18. Moderate to occasional heavy rain
will persist. Between 0.25 and 0.5 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Northern Farmington, Aztec, Flora Vista, Cedar Hill and La Plata.

This includes Highway 550 between Mile Markers 160 and 162...and near
Mile Marker 166...and between Mile Markers 168 and 174.

This includes the following low water crossings...
Hill-N-Dale Drive at Hood Arroyo, East Crestwood Drive at Hood Arroyo
and Jack Rabbit Junction.

This includes the following recreation areas...
Glade Run Recreation Area, Jackson Lake Wildlife Area and Aztec Ruins
National Monument.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Do not enter or cross flowing water or water of unknown depth.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 4:15 PM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Okeechobee County in east central Florida...

* Until 415 PM EST.

* At 210 PM EST, local law enforcement reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 4 and 7 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Treasure Island, Okeechobee, Four Seasons Estates, Taylor Creek,
Whispering Pines, Okeechobee Airport and Basswood Estates.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 12:03PM MST until November 1 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 3:00 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 3:00 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Gila County in east central Arizona...
Navajo County in north central Arizona...
Apache County in northeastern Arizona...

* Until 300 PM MST.

* At 1203 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling across the warned area. Between 0.75 and 1.25
inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Whiteriver, Springerville, Eagar, St. Johns, North Fork, Canyon
Day, Rainbow City, Seven Mile, East Fork, McNary, Turkey Creek,
Alpine, Fort Apache, Greer, Vernon, Concho, Nahata Dziil, Feaster
and Tenney Pond.

This includes the following highways...
State Route 261 between mile markers 395 and 412. State Route 260
between mile markers 361 and 398. Highway 60 between mile markers 358
and 401. State Route 73 between mile markers 326 and 353. Highway 191
161 between mile markers 316 and 366. State Route 61 between mile
markers 357 and 430. State Route 473 between mile markers 0 and 10.
State Route 373 between mile markers 386 and 390. Highway 191 between
mile markers 248 and 253. Highway 180 191 between mile markers 371
and 433. Highway 180 between mile markers 336 and 368. State Route
273 between mile markers 378 and 396.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Winn Campground, Buffalo Crossing Campground, Rolfe C. Hoyer
Campground, Deer Creek Campground, Raccoon Campground, Rainbow
Campground, Cutthroat Campground, Diamond Rock Campground, Horse
Springs Campground, Grayling Campground, Luna Lake Campground,
Brookchar Campground, Benny Creek Campground, Aspen Campground - East
Fork Black River, Alpine Divide Campground, Apache Trout Campground,
Alpine Divide Campground, Diamond Creek Campground, Diamond Rock
Campground, Hoyer Campground, Lyman Lake Campground, Elderberry
Spring Campground, Deer Creek (East Fork - Black River) Campground,
Horse Springs Campground & Group Ramada, West Fork Campground, Nelson
Reservoir Recreation Area and White Mountain Ultalight Flightpark.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Little Colorado River, Bear Cienega Creek, Pine Creek, Thompson
Creek, Zui River, White River, Black River, and Carrizo Wash.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.
