flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Prescott Valley, Chino Valley, Cottonwood, Camp Verde, Williamson
Valley, Clarkdale, Paulden, Williams, Ash Fork, Jerome, Agua Fria
National Monument, Cherry, Drake, Flower Pot, Kaibab Estates West
and Perkinsville.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 40 between mile markers 131 and 158. State Route 260
between mile markers 212 and 219. State Route 69 between mile markers
284 and 290. Business Interstate 40 near mile marker 146. Interstate
17 between mile markers 269 and 287. State Route 89 between mile
markers 322 and 363. State Route 89A between mile markers 322 and
348.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Potato Patch Campground, Playground Group Campground, Dogtown Lake
Campground, Powell Springs Campground, Bill Williams Campground,
Texaco Hillside RV Campground and Mountainview Park.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Sycamore Creek, Ash Creek, Big Chino Wash, Williamson Valley Wash,
Ash Fork Draw and the Verde River from near Paulden to Perkinsville.

muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 3:00 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 3:00 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 300 PM MST.

* At 1139 AM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 2.5
inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* For Dry Beaver Creek at Dry Beaver Creek Near Rimrock:
At 11:30am the stage was 11.93 feet.
Flood Stage is 12.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 12.38 feet is expected around 12:00pm Sunday.
Impacts:
At 12.0 feet: Minor flooding near stream banks. Old bridge
affected.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Village of Oak Creek, Lake Montezuma, McGuireville, Munds Mountain
Wilderness and Bell Rock.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 17 between mile markers 292 and 294...and between mile
markers 299 and 303. State Route 179 between mile markers 299 and
307.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Rarick Canyon, Dry Beaver Creek, Rattlesnake Canyon, and Beaver
Creek.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 11:02AM MST until November 1 at 2:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 2:15 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 2:15 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 215 PM MST.

* At 1102 AM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 3 inches
of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* For Wet Beaver Creek at Wet Beaver Creek Near Rimrock:
At 9:45am the stage was 13.45 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 14.62 feet is expected at 6:00pm Sunday.
Impacts:
At 8.0 feet: Low water crossings impassable, water begins to exceed
banks and inundate low lying areas.
At 9.5 feet: Water begins to impact residential structures along
Rim Rock Drive and Beaver Vista in Lake Montezuma.
At 10.5 feet: Water likely impacting first ground level of
residences along Rim Rock Drive and Beaver Vista, water begins to
directly impact Rim Rock Drive and Beaver Vista.
At 12.0 feet: Widespread inundation of residences along Wet Beaver
Creek.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lake Montezuma, Rimrock, Montezuma Castle National Monument,
McGuireville, Montezuma Well, Lawrence Crossing, Crane Petroglyph
Heritage Site, Bell Crossing/The Crack and Wet Beaver Wilderness.

This includes Interstate 17 between mile markers 291 and 293.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Wet Beaver Creek Campground.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Wet Beaver Creek Day Use Area and Bell Crossing "The Crack".

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Rarick Canyon, Dry Beaver Creek, Verde River, Long Canyon, Walker
Creek, Beaver Creek and Russell Wash.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 11:00AM MST until November 1 at 2:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 2:15 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 2:15 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 215 PM MST.

* At 1100 AM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling across the warned area. Between 1.75 and 3
inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* For Oak Creek at Cornville:
At 10:00am the stage was 16.39 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.0 feet.
Forecast: The creek is expected to crest around 12:00pm Sunday.
Impacts:
At 12.0 feet: Significant flooding of RV park near Page Springs Rd.
...
For Oak Creek at Oak Creek at Sedona:
At 10:45am the stage was 13.8 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 16.08 feet is expected at 11:00am Sunday.
Impacts:
At 13.0 feet: Stream reaches terrace under Tlaquepaque bridge. Low
water crossings closed.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sedona, Cornville, Page Springs, Indian Gardens, Pine Flats, Uptown
Sedona, Red Rock State Park, Slide Rock State Park, West Fork of
Oak Creek, Red Rock-Secret Mountain Wilderness, Cathedral Rock, and
Oak Creek Vista Overlook.

This includes the following highways...
State Route 179 between mile markers 310 and 313. State Route 89A
between mile markers 373 and 390.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Manzanita Campground, Pine Flat Campground, Cave Springs Campground
and Windmill Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Pumphouse Wash, Slide Rock, Encinoso, Grasshopper Point, Midgely
Bridge, Buddha Beach "Red Rock Crossing", Crescent Moon Ranch and
Mormons Crossing.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Dry Creek, Oak Creek, Turkey Creek, West Fork Oak Creek and Spring
Creek.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 12:58PM EST until November 1 at 2:15PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 2:15 PM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 2:15 PM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Okeechobee County in east central Florida...

* Until 215 PM EST.

* At 1258 PM EST, local law enforcement reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 6 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Treasure Island, Okeechobee, Taylor Creek, Four Seasons Estates,
Okeechobee Airport, Whispering Pines and Basswood Estates.

Law enforcement reports portions of SR 70 and US 441 in and around
the City of Okeechobee are impassable. Motorists should avoid these
roads. Water was also entering structures.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

info.description:
At 1052 AM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
that heavy rain was falling across the warned area. Between 1 and 2
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch
are possible in the warned area. Multiple swift water rescues have
been reported, use caution when driving. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash
flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Tucson, Catalina, Oro Valley, Marana, Oracle, Casas Adobes, Drexel
Heights, Flowing Wells, Saddlebrooke, South Tucson, Three Points,
Saddlebrooke Ranch, Pascua Pueblo Yaqui Reservation, Tortolita, San
Xavier Community, Tucson Mountain Park, Saguaro National Park West,
Tucson Estates, Valencia West and Catalina Foothills.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Manville Rd at Brawley Wash, 1st Ave north of Fort Lowell Rd, Stone
Ave at Mabel St, Twin Peaks Rd between Sanders and Sandario,
Silverbell Rd near Ina Rd, Camino De La Tierra at the Rillito River,
Camino de Oeste from Sweetwater to Gates Pass, Ironwood Hills Dr from
Shannon to Camino de Oeste, Mark Rd from Jeffery Rd to Los Reales Rd,
Mission Rd from Valencia Rd to San Xavier Rd, Overton Rd at Canada
del Oro, Sunset Rd west of Camino de Oeste, E Wilds Rd at the Canada
del Oro and Black Wash at S Camino de Oeste.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Alambre Wash, Rillito River, South Mendoza Wash, Santa Cruz River,
Soto Wash, Altar Wash, Chalk Creek, West Branch Santa Cruz River,
Chico, Arroyo, Mendoza Wash, Old Junction Wash, Sutherland Wash,
Blanco Wash, Chirreon Wash, Banner Wash, Indian Well Wash, Big
Wash, Oro, Caada del, Robles Wash, Los, Champurrado Wash, Demetrie
Wash, Brawley Wash, Guild Wash and Cerro Prieto Wash.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 2:00 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
At 1049 AM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
that heavy rain was falling across the warned area. Between 1 and 2
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch
are possible in the warned area. Multiple swift water rescues have
been reported, use caution when driving. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash
flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Tucson, Sahuarita, Green Valley, Oracle, Mammoth, Tubac,
Davis-Monthan Air Force Base, Tanque Verde, Vail, Corona De Tucson,
South Tucson, San Manuel, East Sahuarita, San Xavier Community,
Sonoita, Mount Lemmon/Summerhaven, Saguaro National Park East,
Sabino Canyon Recreation Area and Catalina Foothills.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Harrison Rd at Pantano Wash, Agua Caliente Wash from Soldier Trl to
Fort Lowell, Country Club Rd at Franco Wash, Wentworth Rd at Tanque
Verde Wash, Tanque Verde Loop Rd at Tanque Verde Wash, Old Spanish
Trl at Rincon Creek, Houghton Rd from I-10 & Sahuarita Rd, Santa
Clara Ave at El Vado Wash, Escalante Rd at Atterbury Wash, River Rd
at San Pedro River, Sahuarita Rd west of Wilmot Rd, Alamo Wash
between Speedway and Grant, Andrada Rd east of Wentworth Rd, Camino
Loma Alta at Rincon Creek, Drexel Rd east of Alvernon Way, Freeman Rd
between Broadway and Old Spanish Trail, Limberlost Rd from Soilder
Trail to Homestead Ave, Old Spanish Trail at Jeremy Wash, Old Vail
COnnection Rd at Franco Wash, Calle Rinconada Rd from Andrada Rd to
Sahuarita Rd and Snyder Rd from Kolb Rd to Sabino Canyon Rd.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Ash Creek, Hot Springs Canyon, Rillito River, Agua Caliente Wash,
Peitas Wash, Guijas Wash, Las, Chimney Rock Creek, Santa Cruz
River, Mud Spring Canyon, Redfield Canyon, Sonoita Creek, Ventana
Canyon Wash, Mescal Arroyo, Sabino Creek, Bear Creek, Bird Canyon,
Long Hollow, Martinez Wash, Chico, Arroyo, West Branch Santa Cruz
River, Squaw Creek, Aravaipa Creek, Josephine Canyon, Teran Wash,
Esperero Wash, Old Junction Wash, Paddys River, Coyote Wash, Apache
Canyon, Pantano Wash, Soza Wash, Sutherland Wash, Cienega Creek,
Sycamore Creek, Papalote Wash, Tanque Verde Wash, Redrock Creek,
Rincon Creek, Gardner Canyon, Saucito Wash, Paige Creek, Box Canyon
Wash, Agua Verde Creek, Deer Creek, Fortynine Wash, Oak Creek, San
Pedro River, Bollen Wash, Sopori Wash, Stratton Wash, Oro, Caada
del, Rattlesnake Creek, Fourmile Creek, Turkey Creek, Arivaca
Creek, Klondyke Wash, Demetrie Wash, Bolas Blancas Wash, Buehman
Canyon, Gibb Wash, Alder Wash and Sheep Camp Wash.

deaths occur in vehicles.

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 1:45 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 1:45 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 145 PM MST.

* At 1038 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the
warned area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Bagdad, Congress, Yarnell, Wilhoit, Peeples Valley, Iron Springs,
Kirkland, Skull Valley, Copper Basin, Hawkins, Stanton, and
Wagoner.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 93 between mile markers 149 and 196. State Route 96 between
mile markers 0 and 21. State Route 71 between mile markers 90 and
109. State Route 89 between mile markers 258 and 302. State Route 97
between mile markers 156 and 166.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Yavapai Campground, Yavapai Campground, Alto Pit OHV and Cayuse
Picnic Area.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Kirkland Creek, Spence Creek, Cherry Creek, Yarnell Creek, Tank
Creek, Poplar Wash, Amazon Gulch, Copper Creek, Skull Valley Wash,
Minnehaha Creek, Peoples Canyon, East Antelope Creek, Alkali Wash,
Logan Wash, Castle Creek, , Finch Wash, Iron Springs Wash, Dead
Mexican Creek, Iron Spring Wash, Black Canyon Wash, Waterman Creek,
Willow Creek, Mescal Creek, Little Sycamore Wash, Boulder Creek,
and Weaver Creek.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Gila County in east central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 430 PM MST.

* At 1030 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the
warned area. Between 1.75 and 2.75 inches of rain have fallen.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Camp Verde, Verde Lakes, Mountain View Estates, Rockin' River Ranch
State Park, Indian Maiden Falls and West Clear Creek Wilderness.

This includes State Route 260 between mile markers 223 and 239.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Clear Creek Group Campgrounds.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Bull Pen Day Use Area, West Clear Creek near the campground and
Indian Maiden Falls.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Beaver Creek, West Clear Creek, Verde River, Fossil Creek, Walker
Creek, Bull Run Creek, Long Canyon and Russell Wash.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Gila County in east central Arizona...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Navajo County in north central Arizona...
Apache County in northeastern Arizona...

* Until 430 PM MST Sunday.

* At 1027 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the
warned area. Between 0.75 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Winslow, Holbrook, Heber-Overgaard, Dilkon, Ganado, Kykotsmovi
Village, Snowflake, Taylor, Joseph City, Pinon, First Mesa, Leupp,
Hotevilla-Bacavi, Shongopovi, Keams Canyon, Second Mesa,
Greasewood, Nazlini, Pinedale, and Winona.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 40 between mile markers 210 and 322. State Route 260
between mile markers 286 and 330. Business Interstate 40 between mile
markers 252 and 289. State Route 377 between mile markers 0 and 33.
State Route 277 between mile markers 306 and 336. State Route 77
between mile markers 353 and 408. State Route 264 between mile
markers 365 and 455. State Route 99 between mile markers 23 and 71.
State Route 87 between mile markers 292 and 406. Highway 191 between
mile markers 390 and 437. Highway 180 between mile markers 308 and
336.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Rock Crossing Campground, Chevelon Crossing Campground, Chevelon
Canyon Lake Campground, Forest Road 237 Camping Area, Lewis Canyon
Group Campground, Blue Ridge Campground, Black Canyon Rim Campground,
Canyon Point Campground, Ashurst Lake Campgrounds, Homolovi State
Park Campground, Forked Pine Campground, Elks Group Campground,
Larson Ridge Camping Area, Camp Shadow Pines, Black Canyon Lake
Recreation Area, Tall Timbers County Park, Hunt Park, McHood Park,
Sacred Heart Park and Winslow City Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Clear Creek Reservoir.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Oraibi Wash, Chevelon Canyon, Canyon Diablo, Clear Creek, Puerco
River, Turkey Creek, Dinnebito Wash, Keams Canyon Wash, Jacks
Canyon, Jeddito Wash, Polacca Wash, Carrizo Creek, Show Low Creek,
and Leroux Wash.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Gila County in east central Arizona...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Navajo County in north central Arizona...

* Until 600 PM MST Sunday.

* At 1007 AM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches
of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Cibecue, Young, Cibecue Airport, Chediski Peak, Brushy Top
Mountain, Pendleton Mesa, Grasshopper Butte, Sierra Ancha
Wilderness, Cibeque Falls, Buck Peak, Buck Mountain, and Valley
View Point.

This includes the following highways...
State Route 260 near mile marker 284. State Route 288 between mile
markers 273 and 311.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Gentry Campground, Airplane Flat Campground, Reynolds Creek
Campground, Rose Creek Campground, Coon Creek Campground, Colcord
Ridge Campground, Forest Road 9512E Camping Area, Upper Canyon Creek
Campground, Valentine Ridge Campground and Elks Youth Camp.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Cibeque Falls.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Foot Canyon, Canyon Creek, Deer Springs Canyon, Bear Creek, Day
School Wash, V Eighteen Wash, Chevelon Canyon, Oak Creek, C One
Wash, Jumpoff Canyon, Spring Creek, Cibecue Creek, Salt Creek, Mud
Creek, Black Canyon and Carrizo Creek.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

Las zonas ya inundadas volverán a inundarse; otras también podrían verse afectadas. No cruce corrientes de agua. Refugio en McGee Park. No espere: prepare su mochila de emergencia y esté listo para salir.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 11:46AM EST until November 1 at 1:15PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

parameter.name: NWSheadline
parameter.value: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 115 PM EST THIS AFTERNOON FOR SOUTHEASTERN OKEECHOBEE COUNTY

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 1:15 PM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 1:15 PM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
At 1146 AM EST, local law enforcement reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 5 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Treasure Island, Okeechobee, Taylor Creek, Four Seasons Estates,
Okeechobee Airport, Whispering Pines and Basswood Estates.

Law enforcement reports portions of State Road 70 and US 441 in and
around the City of Okeechobee are impassable. Motorists should avoid
these roads. Water was also entering structures.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 4:45 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Paria River in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 445 PM MST Sunday.

* At 941 AM MST, a river gauge on the Paria River in southern Utah
reported a rapid rise from heavy rain over the Paria River. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Paria River.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Paria River.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lees Ferry and Vermilion Cliffs National Monument.

This includes the Colorado River near mile marker 0.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Lees Ferry Camp Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Paria River and Colorado River.
info.instruction:
Get out of the Paria River slot canyon! Flood waters will flow down
the Paria River, reaching the confluence with the Colorado River at
Lees Ferry between 5 PM and 8 PM tonight.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 12:15 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Gila County in east central Arizona...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* Until 1215 PM MST.

* At 910 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1.25 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.5 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Four Peaks, Canyon Lake, Saguaro Lake and Tonto Basin.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 8:20AM MST until November 1 at 11:15AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 11:15 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 11:15 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 1115 AM MST.

* At 820 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned
area. Between 1.25 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* For Wet Beaver Creek at Wet Beaver Creek Near Rimrock:
At 7:45am the stage was 11.32 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.5 feet.


Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lake Montezuma, Rimrock, Montezuma Castle National Monument,
McGuireville, Montezuma Well, Lawrence Crossing, Crane Petroglyph
Heritage Site, Bell Crossing/The Crack and Wet Beaver Wilderness.

This includes Interstate 17 between mile markers 291 and 293.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Wet Beaver Creek Campground.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Wet Beaver Creek Day Use Area and Bell Crossing "The Crack".

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Rarick Canyon, Dry Beaver Creek, Verde River, Long Canyon, Walker
Creek, Beaver Creek and Russell Wash.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 8:15AM MST until November 1 at 11:15AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 11:15 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 11:15 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 1115 AM MST.

* At 815 AM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1.25 and 2.5 inches of
rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* For Oak Creek at Cornville:
At 8:00am the stage was 8.88 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.0 feet.

...
For Oak Creek at Oak Creek at Sedona:
At 7:45am the stage was 15.06 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.0 feet.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sedona, Cornville, Jordan, Page Springs, Bignotti, Indian Gardens,
Pine Flats, Uptown Sedona, Sedona Airport, Red Rock State Park,
Slide Rock State Park, West Fork of Oak Creek, Red Rock-Secret
Mountain Wilderness, Cathedral Rock and Oak Creek Vista Overlook.

This includes the following highways...
State Route 179 between mile markers 310 and 313. State Route 89A
between mile markers 373 and 384...and between mile markers 386 and
390.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Manzanita Campground, Pine Flat Campground, Cave Springs Campground
and Windmill Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Pumphouse Wash, Slide Rock, Encinoso, Grasshopper Point, Midgely
Bridge, Buddha Beach "Red Rock Crossing", Crescent Moon Ranch and
Mormons Crossing.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Dry Creek, Verde River, Oak Creek, Turkey Creek, West Fork Oak
Creek and Spring Creek.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 8:14AM MST until November 1 at 11:15AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 11:15 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 11:15 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Gila County in east central Arizona...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* Until 1115 AM MST.

* At 814 AM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling across the warned area. Between 0.75 and 1.25
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1
inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Round Valley, Ballantine Trailhead, Sunflower, Sugarloaf Mountain,
Sycamore Creek, Punkin Center, Tonto Basin and Goldfield Ranch.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 7:26AM MST until November 1 at 10:30AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 10:30 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 10:30 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Gila County in east central Arizona...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* Until 1030 AM MST.

* At 726 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain
has fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rio Verde.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 9:15AM EST until November 1 at 11:15AM EST by NWS Tallahassee FL

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 11:15 AM EST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 11:15 AM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Bay County in the panhandle of Florida...

* Until 1015 AM CST.

* At 815 AM CST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 5 and 8 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Panama City, Springfield, Dirego Park, Millville and Cedar Grove.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 1:49AM MST until November 1 at 4:45AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 4:45 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 4:45 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 445 AM MST.

* At 149 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned
area. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional
rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* For Granite Creek at Prescott:
At 1:30am the stage was 10.61 feet.
Flood Stage is 11.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 11.0 feet: Flooding begins at AC Williams Granite Creek Park
upstream of gage. Low lying patios along Granite Creek in downtown
Prescott flood.
...
For Granite Creek at Granite Creek Near Prescott:
At 1:30am the stage was 7.27 feet.
Flood Stage is 11.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 10.91 feet is expected at 6:00pm Sunday.
Impacts:
At 11.0 feet: Minor flooding. Lowland overflow. Bridge at
Industrial Way overtopped. Trails and bridges in Watson Woods
Riparian Preserve inundated.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Prescott, Chino Valley, Downtown Prescott, Oak Knoll Village,
Whipple, Prescott Regional Airport, Willow Creek Reservoir and
Watson Lake.

This includes the following highways...
State Route 69 between mile markers 294 and 296. State Route 89
between mile markers 309 and 318. State Route 89A between mile
markers 318 and 320.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Acker Park, AC Williams Granite Creek Park and Watson Lake Park.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Willow Creek, Miller Creek, Lynx Creek, Butte Creek, Little Chino
Valley, Agua Fria River, Bottleneck Wash, Granite Creek, Verde
River and Bannon Creek.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

info.description:
FFWLIX

The National Weather Service in New Orleans has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Pearl River County in southern Mississippi...

* Until 200 AM CST.

* At 1249 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 5 and 10 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of West Central Pearl River County.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 12:43AM CDT until November 1 at 2:00AM CST by NWS New Orleans LA

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 2:00 AM CST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 2:00 AM CST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWLIX

The National Weather Service in New Orleans has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Pearl River County in southern Mississippi...

* Until 200 AM CST.

* At 1243 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain in northeast of Crossroads. Between 10 and 17 inches of
rain have fallen. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Crossroads.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 31 at 9:47PM CDT until November 1 at 12:45AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA

parameter.name: NWSheadline
parameter.value: FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY FOR NORTHEAST OF CROSSROADS

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY this area til 12:45 AM CDT. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY is in effect for this area until 12:45 AM CDT. This is an extremely dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWLIX

The National Weather Service in New Orleans has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Pearl River County in southern Mississippi...

* Until 1245 AM CDT.

* At 947 PM CDT, emergency management reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain northeast of Crossroads. Between 6 and 10
inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is already occurring
with ongoing high water rescues and swift moving water covering
multiple roadways.

FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for northeast of Crossroads. This is a
PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. Life
threatening flash flooding of low water crossings, small
creeks and streams, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Crossroads.
info.instruction:
Move to higher ground now! This is an extremely dangerous and
life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are
fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 31 at 6:46PM PDT until October 31 at 9:45PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 9:45 PM PDT. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 9:45 PM PDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWVEF

The National Weather Service in Las Vegas has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Clark County in southern Nevada...

* Until 945 PM PDT.

* At 646 PM PDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.25 and 0.5 inches of
rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
North Las Vegas.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 31 at 8:17PM CDT until October 31 at 10:45PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA

parameter.name: NWSheadline
parameter.value: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 1045 PM CDT THIS EVENING FOR WEST CENTRAL PEARL RIVER COUNTY

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 10:45 PM CDT. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 10:45 PM CDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
At 817 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 4 and 7 inches of rain have
fallen already with heavy rain still ongoing. Additional rainfall
amounts of 2 to 3 inches are possible in the warned area in the next
1-2 hours. Flash flooding is likely ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of West Central Pearl River County.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 31 at 6:15PM CDT until October 31 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA

parameter.name: NWSheadline
parameter.value: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 PM CDT THIS EVENING FOR NORTH CENTRAL JEFFERSON PARISH

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 9:00 PM CDT. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 9:00 PM CDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
At 615 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 6 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses as well as other poor drainage and low-lying
areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Metairie.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 30 at 8:15PM MST until October 30 at 10:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 10:00 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 10:00 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* Until 1000 PM MST.

* At 815 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain has fallen across the warned area, and several
streamflow gauges remain above alarm stage. Between 0.5 and 1.5
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25
inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Scottsdale, Cave Creek, Carefree, Desert Mountain, and Scottsdale
Airport.

This includes the following highways...
AZ Route 101 between mile markers 29 and 36. AZ Route 51 near mile
marker 15.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

info.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* Until 1000 PM MST.

* At 812 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain has fallen across the warned area, and several
streamflow gauges remain above alarm stage. Between 0.5 and 1.5
inches of rain have fallen. Flooding impacts will continue, but no
additional rainfall is expected. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

AZ Route 74 between mile markers 23 and 30. AZ Interstate 17 between
mile markers 217 and 226. AZ Route 303 between mile markers 127 and
136.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 30 at 7:50PM MST until October 30 at 10:45PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 10:45 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 10:45 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* Until 1045 PM MST.

* At 750 PM MST, Local law enforcement reported multiple water
rescues within the warned area. Between 0.75 and 2.25 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Piestewa Peak Park, Camelback Mountain
and Arizona State Fairgrounds.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 8:45 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 8:45 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* Until 845 PM MST.

* At 549 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.50 and 1.25 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Scottsdale, Cave Creek, Carefree, Desert Mountain, and Scottsdale
Airport.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 30 at 5:24PM MST until October 30 at 8:30PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 8:30 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 8:30 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* Until 830 PM MST.

* At 524 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
0.5 and 1.25 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall
amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
New River, Cave Creek and Anthem.

This includes the following highways...
AZ Route 74 between mile markers 23 and 30. AZ Interstate 17 between
mile markers 217 and 226. AZ Route 303 between mile markers 127 and
136.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

flash flooding.

urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Bullhead City, Laughlin, Katherine Landing, Big Bend Rec Area,
Mesquite Creek, Oatman and Mohave Valley.

deaths occur in vehicles.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 30 at 12:43PM PDT until October 30 at 3:45PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 3:45 PM PDT. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 3:45 PM PDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWVEF

The National Weather Service in Las Vegas has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Clark County in southern Nevada...

* Until 345 PM PDT.

* At 1243 PM PDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 1 inch of rain has fallen.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Henderson, Lake Las Vegas, Las Vegas Bay, Las Vegas Bay Campground
and Railroad Pass.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 30 at 2:19AM CDT until October 30 at 4:45AM CDT by NWS Topeka KS

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 4:45 AM CDT. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 4:45 AM CDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWTOP

The National Weather Service in Topeka has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Marshall County in northeastern Kansas...

* Until 445 AM CDT.

* At 219 AM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain in At least one road in the city
of Marysville has been closed due to water covering the road making
it impassable. Between 3.5 and 4 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Marysville.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 30 at 12:00AM CDT until October 30 at 2:45AM CDT by NWS Topeka KS

parameter.name: NWSheadline
parameter.value: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 245 AM CDT EARLY THIS MORNING FOR NORTHERN NEMAHA COUNTY

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 2:45 AM CDT. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 2:45 AM CDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
At midnight CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
3.5 and 4 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
1 to 1.5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Bern.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 29 at 7:56PM MDT until October 29 at 11:00PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 11:00 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 11:00 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
info.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Dona Ana County in south central New Mexico...
Southern Sierra County in south central New Mexico...

* Until 1100 PM MDT.

* At 756 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Garfield.

According to the Elephant Butte Irrigation District, there is
significant water in the watershed upstream of Mcleod Dam with
uncertainty in the integrity of the dam.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

info.headline: Tornado Warning issued October 29 at 6:28PM CDT until October 29 at 7:15PM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: TORNADO WARNING in this area til 7:15 PM CDT. Take shelter now. Check media.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: TORNADO WARNING in this area until 7:15 PM CDT. Take shelter now in a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Check media.

info.description:
TOREWX

The National Weather Service in Austin San Antonio has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Northeastern Kinney County in south central Texas...
West central Uvalde County in south central Texas...

* Until 715 PM CDT.

* At 628 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located over Cline, or 19 miles northwest of Uvalde, moving
northwest at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* This tornadic thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of
northeastern Kinney and west central Uvalde Counties, including the
following locations... Turkey Mountain.
info.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 4:30 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 4:30 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The South Fork burn scar in...
South Central Lincoln County in central New Mexico...

* Until 430 PM MDT.

* At 136 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the South Fork Burn Scar. Up to 1 inch of rain has
fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact Upper Canyon, Brady
Canyon, and Perk Canyon as well as the Cedar Creek, Eagle Creek and
Rio Ruidoso drainages. Impacts will include but are not limited to
all nearby reservoirs, bridges, culverts and roadways. Impacts to
areas along the Rio Ruidoso may extend downstream of Ruidoso Downs.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the South Fork Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
South Fork Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ruidoso, Ruidoso Downs, Alto, Glencoe and Hollywood.
info.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the South Fork Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.
